query: How can businesses improve Yelp user satisfaction?

per_column.name: service_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Service quality is an intervenable lever a business can actually improve; its measured sentiment stands in as the treatment on the service dimension.

per_column.name: food_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Food quality is a configurable operational property a business can change; treated here as an intervenable treatment dimension.

per_column.name: value_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Pricing/value is a settable business decision, hence an intervenable treatment lever.

per_column.name: ambiance_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Ambiance is something a business can deliberately alter (decor, lighting, layout); an intervenable lever.

per_column.name: primary_complaint
per_column.rationale: A summary of what drove dissatisfaction; it is downstream of the underlying dimensions and reflects the outcome perception rather than a common cause of treatment and outcome.

per_column.name: top_positive_driver
per_column.rationale: A derived attribution of which dimension produced positive perception; sits on the causal path to satisfaction, not an adjusting confounder.

per_column.name: satisfaction_driver
per_column.rationale: Combines strength/weakness attribution; a summary along the path to satisfaction, not a common cause of the levers and the outcome.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply plausible intervenable treatment dimensions (service, food, value, ambiance) that a business could actually set or change, satisfying part (a) of the claim. However, the schema contains NO confounders: nothing adjusts for common causes of both a dimension's quality and overall satisfaction (e.g., customer expectations, price tier/segment, location, cuisine type, time/occasion, reviewer strictness). The remaining aspect/driver columns are attribution mediators along the causal path, not confounders, and cannot be used to identify a counterfactual effect. Because part (b) is entirely unmet, the interventional (what-if) claim is not realized.
